data.narrative: Successfully completed Technical Communication Module 03 (Design Documents & RFCs). Authored design-document.md for an API Rate Limiter using a lightweight RFC format, detailing Problem Statement, API Gateway Redis Sliding Window implementation, genuine alternatives, fail-open mitigations, and explicit open questions.

dimension_scores.observation: Analyzed realistic alternatives (in-memory per-instance & fixed-window counters) with genuine pros/cons rather than strawmen.
dimension_scores.evidence: Detailed why in-memory limits fail multi-instance auto-scaling and why fixed windows cause boundary spikes in design-document.md.

dimension_scores.observation: Used plain-language bouncer-at-a-club analogy to explain rate limiting concepts clearly.
dimension_scores.evidence: Framed API rate limiter as a bouncer turning away excess traffic in design-document.md.

dimension_scores.observation: Tailored RFC for senior engineering review by balancing technical trade-offs with business impact.
dimension_scores.evidence: Connected rate limiting infrastructure directly to paid tier SLA revenue and 2 AM incident prevention.

dimension_scores.observation: Followed clear 5-section RFC structure leading with problem before solution.
dimension_scores.evidence: Organized design-document.md into Problem Statement, Proposed Approach, Alternatives Considered, Risks/Mitigations, Open Questions.

dimension_scores.observation: Listed explicit open questions directed to Product and Security teams to unblock implementation.
dimension_scores.evidence: Asked Product for tier thresholds and Security for IP vs Key throttling rules.

strengths: Authored concise lightweight RFC with clear business problem statement, architectural tradeoffs, and fail-open mitigation plan.
Included genuine alternative analysis and targeted open questions for cross-team alignment.
data.recommendation: Maintain clear problem-first framing when communicating incident post-mortems in Module 04.
